q.intro.text: An eighty-dollar jacket is twenty percent off. At the register, you get another ten percent off the sale price. What do you pay? Pick an answer, and say how sure you are.

e.intro.text: Let's work it out in four steps. Press each one, and watch the tape first, then the maths on the board.

e.step0.text: The original price, eighty dollars, is one hundred percent: the whole tape. The first twenty percent is a percent of it.

e.step1.text: Twenty percent off leaves eighty percent of the tape. Eighty percent of eighty dollars is eighty times zero point eight: sixty-four dollars.

e.step2.text: Now sixty-four dollars is the new one hundred percent. Another ten percent off leaves ninety percent of it. Sixty-four times zero point nine is fifty-seven dollars and sixty cents.

e.step3.text: Both steps at once: times zero point eight, and then times zero point nine, is times zero point seven two. You pay seventy-two percent of eighty dollars. That's twenty-eight percent off, not thirty.

e.why.text: Quick check. Why do you pay fifty-seven sixty, and not fifty-six dollars?

e.why.ok.text: Yes. The second ten percent is a percent of sixty-four dollars, not of eighty, so it only takes off six dollars and forty cents.

e.why.adds.text: That adds the percents. But the second ten percent is of the sale price, sixty-four dollars. It takes off six forty, not eight dollars.

e.why.order.text: The order changes nothing here: zero point nine times zero point eight is also zero point seven two. What matters is that the second percent is of a smaller amount.

t.intro.text: A fifty-dollar video game goes up twenty percent. Later, the store cuts the new price by twenty percent. I'll do the first step. Then it's your turn.

t.given.text: Up twenty percent: fifty dollars times one point two is sixty dollars.

t.base.text: The twenty percent cut: which amount is one hundred percent now?

t.base.ok.text: Yes. The cut is a percent of the price at that moment, sixty dollars. That's the new one hundred percent.

t.base.no.text: Fifty dollars was the one hundred percent for the first change. The cut comes after the price went up, so it's twenty percent of sixty dollars.

t.price.text: What is the price after the twenty percent cut?

t.price.ok.text: Right. Sixty dollars times zero point eight is forty-eight dollars.

t.price.adds.text: Not back to fifty. Twenty percent of sixty is twelve dollars: more than the ten dollars it went up. Sixty minus twelve is forty-eight.

t.price.change.text: Twelve dollars is the cut itself. The new price is what's left of the sixty dollars.

t.price.miss.text: Take twenty percent of sixty dollars off, or work out sixty times zero point eight. Try again.

t.net.text: Last step. Compared with the fifty dollars at the start, what is the net change?

t.net.ok.text: Yes. One point two times zero point eight is zero point nine six. The game ends at ninety-six percent of fifty dollars: a four percent decrease.

t.net.adds.text: Up twenty percent and down twenty percent don't cancel. The cut was a percent of a bigger amount. One point two times zero point eight is zero point nine six: a four percent decrease.

t.net.pctof.text: Ninety-six percent is the new price as a percent of the start. The change is the difference from one hundred percent: down four percent.

t.done.text: Back to the jacket. The second ten percent is of sixty-four dollars, so you pay eighty, times zero point eight, times zero point nine: fifty-seven dollars and sixty cents.

p.intro.text: A fifty-dollar pair of headphones. Store A takes twenty percent off, then adds eight percent tax. Store B adds the eight percent tax first, then takes twenty percent off. Ava says: Store A is cheaper, because its tax is on a smaller amount. Is Ava right?

p.build.no.text: Now prove it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.build.yes.text: Let's test it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true, and see where it leads.

p.c1.text: Store A: twenty percent off leaves forty dollars, and eight percent tax on forty dollars makes forty-three dollars and twenty cents.

p.c2.text: Store B: the tax makes fifty-four dollars, and twenty percent off fifty-four also leaves forty-three dollars and twenty cents.

p.c3.text: Both are fifty dollars, times zero point eight, times one point zero eight. The tapes end at the same place. The order doesn't matter, so Ava is wrong.

p.done.text: That's a proof. Every claim has its reason, and the tapes back each one. Two percent changes are two multipliers, and multipliers can go in any order.

p.chip.adds.text: Careful. Twenty percent off and eight percent tax don't make twelve percent off. Each percent is of a different amount. Work out each step.

p.chip.order.text: That's exactly what we're testing. Work out both totals before you decide.

p.chip.coupon.text: That's not true. A ten-dollar coupon is subtracted, not multiplied, so with a coupon the order does matter.

p.chip.other.text: True, but it's the reason for a different line. Which one makes this line true?
